subject: Unable to accept supplier portal invite — conflicting accounts
messages:
From: Joanna Taylor <j.taylor@acmepartners.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Trouble accepting supplier portal invite

Hi Marissa / Ben,

We received the supplier portal invite this morning but when I click the link it bounces me to the sign-in page and then immediately back to the invite with an error: "Account already exists with a different identity provider". Our identity team uses Okta (we're on passkeys for some users). We do have a legacy Google account tied to the same email from an old corporate domain; not sure if that is clashing.

Screenshot attached (acme_invite_screenshot.png) — the error includes the string "identity_collision" and shows a tenant of "acme-safepath" in the URL. Can you advise? We need to get the portal access in order to upload our W-9 and complete onboarding by end of week.

Thanks,
Joanna Taylor
Head of Finance Ops
Acme Partners

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Taylor <j.taylor@acmepartners.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting supplier portal invite

Hi Joanna — thanks for the report and the screenshot. A few quick asks so we can triage:

- Can you confirm the exact email address you clicked the invite with? (Is it j.taylor@acmepartners.com or a different alias?)
- Please paste the full invite URL (or forward the invite email) — I need the invite_token query param and tenant id.
- Try incognito/private browser & clear cookies; sometimes a stale SSO session causes the redirect loop.

Workarounds we can do while we investigate:
- We can create a supplier record manually and send a DocuSign W-9 request to the email you specify.
- If you prefer, we can reissue the invite with a flag that forces an identity link step (engineering support required).

I've opened an internal ticket (SUP-4572) and will escalate if this looks like an identity-provider mapping issue. If you can forward me the invite HTML (invite_link.html) and any additional logs/screenshots that would help.

Best,
Ben Carter
Partner Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Joanna Taylor <j.taylor@acmepartners.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting supplier portal invite

Ben — attaching the invite HTML (invite_link.html) and a slightly larger screenshot. The invite URL is: https://supplier.redwood.ai/invite?tenant=acme-safepath&invite_token=eyJ0eXAi...

When I try to accept it I see the message: "SSO identity collision: existing_provider=google, incoming_provider=okta-passkey". My company recently enabled Okta passkeys but our DNS/SCIM migration left some legacy Google identities floating around.

If a manual supplier record would unblock us fastest, please go ahead; otherwise happy to wait for a fix. We need the W-9 flow open so accounting can process the first PO.

Joanna

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Joanna Taylor <j.taylor@acmepartners.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting supplier portal invite — escalation

Looping in Laura and escalating to platform engineering. Summary for the ticket: Acme Partners invite (tenant=acme-safepath) failing acceptance due to SSO provider collision between legacy google identity and incoming okta-passkey. External provided invite_token and screenshot.

Proposed plan:
1) Engineering: check identity mapping for invite_token and tenant bind. If possible, rebind incoming Okta identity to existing supplier record or allow an "identity-link" step on the acceptance flow.
2) Short-term: Ben / Ops can create a manual supplier entry and send a DocuSign W-9 to Joanna to avoid blocking PO creation.
3) Avoid creating duplicate supplier profiles that would block future invoices. If manual creation is done, mark as pending-merge and keep the invite_token in case we can retroactively link.

Ticket: SUP-4572 — see logs: https://internal.redwood.ai/logs/SUP-4572 (engineering only).

Laura — assigning to you to coordinate SLA for this account (they asked for end-of-week).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Taylor <j.taylor@acmepartners.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting supplier portal invite — resolution steps

Hi Joanna — quick update: engineering identified the identity collision and merged the Okta provider mapping into the existing supplier identity for tenant acme-safepath. You should be able to accept the invite now. Steps:

1) Open an incognito/private browser window.
2) Paste this invite URL (same as before).
3) When prompted, complete the Okta passkey sign-in.

If you still hit a problem, reply and we'll reissue a one-time acceptance link.

I've also created a manual supplier record temporarily and sent a DocuSign W-9 request to your inbox (DocuSign: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABCD-1234). If you prefer to accept the portal invite instead, ignore the DocuSign. Attached is a copy of the W-9 request (w9_request.pdf) for your records.

Thanks for the patience and sorry for the churn — we'll follow up to ensure your first PO can be issued.

Best,
Ben Carter
Partner Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference
